title: Interpreting forecasts
text: Weather forecasts are model estimates at a grid-cell scale. Local terrain and storms can differ. Uncertainty generally grows with forecast lead time. An unavailable alert feed does not imply no hazards.

title: Crop water demand
text: Reference evapotranspiration ET0 multiplied by a crop coefficient estimates crop evapotranspiration. Net irrigation also depends on effective precipitation and soil-water storage; field measurements and local agronomic advice are needed.

title: Air-quality model interpretation
text: CAMS air-quality fields are numerical model estimates. US AQI bands are 0–50 Good, 51–100 Moderate, 101–150 Unhealthy for sensitive groups, 151–200 Unhealthy, 201–300 Very unhealthy and above 300 Hazardous.

title: Flood information
text: Never infer a clear road from absent incident data. Rainfall alone cannot establish whether a road is flooded. Use authoritative warnings and local road closures; do not enter floodwater.

title: Visibility
text: Visibility forecasts cannot establish the exact distance to a patch of fog. Reduce speed to match actual conditions; use local traffic advisories. GPS coordinates contain no temperature or visibility observations.

title: Climate versus weather
text: Historical reanalysis combines model information with observations. Climate projections describe statistics under assumptions and are not exact day-to-day forecasts.
